clock_fraction_30: Indonesian toward-the-hour half: "setengah <H>" == the half *before* hour H,
three), NOT 03:30. This is the German-style toward-hour reading, corroborated
across Indonesian usage. KBBI (Kamus Besar Bahasa Indonesia) gives "setengah
jam" == 30 minutes (half an hour); the toward-hour clock reading ("setengah
tiga" == 02:30) is corroborated across Indonesian usage sources -- a
DBP/KBBI-canonical clock-reading passage was not obtained, stated honestly.
The quarter (suku/seperempat) is deliberately omitted: its direction is
UNCONFIRMED (documented follow-up), so only the unambiguous half is added.
clock_meridiem_night: The NIGHT daypart is a midnight-crossing BAND in colloquial clock usage,
not a uniform +12 PM shift: "pukul satu malam"/"jam satu malam" (one at
night) is 01:00, "pukul sebelas malam" (eleven at night) is 23:00, twelve
is midnight 00:00.  Small hours 1..5 stay AM, evening hours 6..11 are PM,
twelve is midnight (band-split in resolver _clock_hms).  Evening "malam"
opens at 18:00 (CLDR id night [18:00, 00:00), transcribed in chronologia/
dayparts.py); the small hours read as "malam" colloquially.  Source:

"nanti malam" = tonight (band still ahead today); "nanti pagi" = tomorrow
marker_daypart_past: Deictic daypart selector: the NEAREST PAST occurrence of a time-of-day band.
"tadi pagi" = this (past) morning (today, already begun); "tadi malam" = last
night (tonight's band has not begun, so the nearest past night is yesterday's).

weekday_0: Indonesian names a weekday with the classifier "hari" in front of it: KBBI
defines Senin as "hari ke-2 dalam jangka waktu satu minggu" and every other
day name the same way, so "hari Senin" is one name and not the noun "hari"
followed by something else (KBBI, Badan Pengembangan dan Pembinaan Bahasa).
Listing the classifier form as a surface is what keeps "setiap hari Senin"
from being read as "setiap hari" (every day) with the weekday discarded;
bare "setiap hari" still means daily, because both readings are real.
